title: baseline vs hypothesis-first discovery
kind: P1 single-variable prompt/workflow experiment; discovery only
hypothesis: The current one-pass broad prompt often returns no candidate or an adjacent issue. A structured understand -> enumerate -> counterexample -> check -> candidates prompt should increase reference candidate recall without increasing fixed-side same-issue alarms or lowering completion.
selection_reason: The six development cases used by r0/r1/r2; frozen before this experiment. Both buggy and fixed sides and all 18 r0 input windows are used.
metrics: reference candidate recall on the buggy side
extra candidate count (not automatically false positives)
adoption: At least two more correctly identified reference pairs than baseline, with no increase in fixed-side same-issue alarms and no lower completed window count. A single repetition is exploratory; repeat before adoption.
holdout: Only if the development result meets the adoption condition; use the four prepared holdout cases in a separate phase and budget.
scope: Discovery only; no Agent-generated tests, no evidence engine, no official tests/labels/opposite version in the Agent input. Known-location windows; not a full-repo or new-sample score. All failures and requests retained.
